source_refs.quoted_text:
The selected rate is a per-planned-star yield: its denominator is all 40
planned stars, including the 8 that screening removed. The 8 removed stars
contribute 0 detections to the numerator because their light curves were
not assessed for transit-like dips, so the reported rate is a lower bound
on the yield that fully usable observations of all 40 stars would have
produced. No claim is made here about the detection rate among the 32
retained stars alone.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: To falsify a no-issue verdict I searched for any place where a 32-denominator (retained-subset) rate is presented as the complete-domain result. The selected result and all per-field rates use planned counts (10 per field, 40 total) as denominators; I recomputed 6/40 = 0.1500 and the per-field rates (1/10, 2/10, 1/10, 2/10) from the raw CSV and they match. I also checked whether the lower-bound framing could conceal a subset-for-domain substitution: the removed stars all carry transit_dip_flag=NA in the CSV, so treating them as contributing 0 detections while stating this explicitly as a lower bound is a disclosed limitation, not a retained-subset denominator substitution. No instance of the in-scope issue class survived this check.
